judged_text: deleteEvent's new find is inverted: when externalCalendarId is falsy, `find((cal) => cal.externalId === undefined)` never matches, so the destinationCalendar fallback that the old code used is dropped and the delete targets primary. Cancelling a booking that has a destinationCalendar but no persisted externalCalendarId on the reference deletes the event from the organizer's primary calendar (or fails with 404/410 on the wrong calendar), leaving the real calendar event orphaned.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed the fallback calendar selection from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy. When `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null`, this becomes `find(cal => cal.externalId === undefined)`, which will typically return `undefined`, dropping the prior destinationCalendar fallback. That makes the subsequent calendarId selection fall back to primary (or an incorrect default), matching the finding’s described orphaned-event/wrong-calendar deletion risk.
